div.head: III Eg 4
div.ab: ⁊ se þe oðerne mid wóge forseggan wille, þæt he aþor oððe feo oððe feore þe wyrsa sý, gyf þonne se oðer geunsoðian mæge, þæt him man onsecgan wolde, si he his tungan scyldig, butan he hine mid his were forgylde.

⁊ se ðe oðerne mid wó forsecgan wille, þæt he aðer oððe feo oððe feore (uel freme) þe wyrsa sy, gif þonne se oðer þæt geunsoðian mæge, þæt him mon onsecgan wolde, sy he his tungan scyldig, buton he hine mid his were forgylde.
Et qui aliquem iniuste superdicere presumet, unde uita uel commodo peior sit, lingue sue reus erit, si accusatus se idoneare et accusationem falsare poterit, nisi se redimat wera sua.

[Be ðon ðe mon oþerne forsecgaþ.] [Ld] And se þe oðerne mid woge forseccan wille, þæt he aðor oððe feo oððe freme þe wyrsa sy, gif þonne se oðer ðæt geunsoðian mæge þæt him man onsecgan wolde, sy he his tungan scildig, buton he hine mid his were forgilde.

And if anyone seeks to accuse another man falsely, so that he is injured either in property or in reputation, and if the second man can refute the charge which the first has sought to bring against him, the first shall forfeit his tongue, unless he redeem himself with his wergeld.

(Davon, dass jemand einen verleumdet. Ld) Und wer einen andern mit Bosheit verklagen will, so dass dieser entweder an Gut oder Leben (Gedeihen A D G2) dadurch geschädigt wird: wenn dann der andere [Verklagte] als unwahr erweisen kann, was jener über ihn klagen wollte, so sei jener seine Zunge [zu verlieren] schuldig, ausser wenn er sich durch sein Wergeld auslöst.

(Of slandering someone. Ld) And whoever wishes to accuse another maliciously, so that the latter is harmed thereby either in property or in life (prosperity, A D G2): if the other [accused] can then prove false what that man wished to charge him with, let that man be liable [to lose] his tongue, unless he redeems himself with his wergild.
div.note: A has ‘unriht’ in the margin in a 14th-c. hand, and ‘uel freme’ written above ‘feore’ by the scribe. Liebermann compares Af 32.
